Longevity Noodles

Served at: New Year's Day · Lunar New Year (Chunjie)

Serves 4Prep 15 minCook 15 min

Longevity Noodles are a traditional Chinese dish served during New Year's Day and Lunar New Year (Chunjie) celebrations. These noodles symbolize long life and good health, making them an essential part of the festive meal. They are typically stir-fried or served in broth and enjoyed by families to usher in prosperity and longevity for the year ahead.

Ingredients

  • 8 oz (225 g) fresh Chinese egg noodles or long wheat noodles
  • 2 tablespoons vegetable oil
  • 3 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 cup (100 g) shredded carrots
  • 1 cup (100 g) sliced shiitake mushrooms
  • 1 cup (100 g) snow peas, trimmed
  • 2 green onions, sliced
  • 2 tablespoons soy sauce
  • 1 tablespoon oyster sauce
  • 1 teaspoon sesame oil
  • 1/2 teaspoon sugar
  • 1/4 teaspoon white pepper
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) chicken or vegetable broth

Method

  1. Bring a large pot of water to a boil and cook the noodles according to package instructions until just tender. Drain and set aside.
  2. Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat.
  3. Add minced garlic and stir-fry for about 30 seconds until fragrant.
  4. Add shredded carrots, sliced shiitake mushrooms, and snow peas. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
  5. Add the cooked noodles to the wok and toss to combine with the vegetables.
  6. Pour in soy sauce, oyster sauce, sesame oil, sugar, white pepper, and chicken broth. Stir-fry everything together for 2-3 minutes until the noodles are well coated and heated through.
  7. Add sliced green onions and give a final toss before serving immediately.

Tips

  • Use fresh, long noodles to symbolize longevity; avoid cutting them before cooking.
  • For a vegetarian version, substitute oyster sauce with mushroom sauce and use vegetable broth.
  • Add cooked shrimp, chicken, or tofu for extra protein and variety.
